author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both surfaces
summary: The veterinarian directory page and its machine-readable companion route each accept an optional specialty to filter on, presenting only veterinarians who hold it; the page stays paginated. The machine-readable route is reinstated as a supported surface. Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive.
acceptance_criteria: The directory page filtered to a held specialty lists only veterinarians holding it, a page at a time.
The machine-readable route filtered to a held specialty returns only veterinarians holding it.
Matching is on the whole specialty name and disregards letter case; a value matching only the start of a name matches no veterinarian.
A specialty naming no veterinarian returns the ordinary page or document with no veterinarians, as a successful response rather than an error, on both surfaces.
A blank or spaces-only specialty filters nothing and returns the same result as omitting the filter, on both surfaces.
With no specialty given, both surfaces behave as they do without the filter.
The machine-readable route is a supported surface carrying the specialty filter as its first capability.
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope; NG-9 narrows only to permit filtering by an already-displayed attribute (specialty).
notes: REQ-VET-003 minted fresh; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn in Superseded and its id is not reused. HTML-surface filter warrants its own requirement rather than extending REQ-VET-001: filtering is a distinct capability from publishing the directory, and the matching semantics are identical across the HTML page and the machine-readable route, so both surfaces stay under one coherent requirement. NG-9 narrowed accordingly. Slice cuts controller + repository + view + tests in one vertical.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Rides existing patterns with a small adjustment on each layer. Repository: add a Spring Data derived-query method to VetRepository (Repository pattern, system-design § Contracts) traversing the Vet -> specialties -> Specialty.name path with case-insensitive whole-name equality. Controller: both handlers gain an optional specialty request param, normalized and branched exactly as OwnerController.processFindForm normalizes the owner last-name search. No new pattern, module, or ADR. One doc reconciliation applied: the Known Defects row asserting the machine-readable /vets route 'serves no requirement... pending removal' is removed, since the PRD amendment (2026-08-04) reinstates it as a supported surface under REQ-VET-003.
integration_points: Persistence filter shape: add derived queries on VetRepository keyed on the specialty name property path. Paged HTML surface needs Page<Vet> findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable); JSON surface needs Collection<Vet> findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String). The 'SpecialtiesName' path traverses the @ManyToMany from Vet to Specialty (which extends NamedEntity, exposing name); 'IgnoreCase' plus equality (not StartingWith) gives the case-insensitive WHOLE-name match the PRD mandates, so a prefix matches no vet by construction.

Pagination composition: VetController.findPaginated(page) currently calls vetRepository.findAll(pageable). Thread the normalized specialty through it and branch: blank -> findAll(pageable) (today's behavior); non-blank -> findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(specialty, pageable). Page/PageRequest math is unchanged; totalPages/totalElements come from the filtered Page so pagination already applies to the filtered set.

JSON surface: showResourcesVetList gains the same normalized param and the same branch over the non-paged pair (findAll() vs findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(specialty)); the Vets wrapper root element is unchanged.

HTML pagination links: vetList.html hardcodes th:href='@{/vets.html?page=N}' on every page/first/prev/next/last control. Filtered paging past page 1 would silently drop the specialty unless each link carries it — add the specialty query param (e.g. via a template variable) to every page link so the filter survives navigation.

patterns.description: Empty/blank normalization precedent to MIRROR: processFindForm takes the raw search value, maps null -> "", else strip()s it, and treats blank as the no-filter case. Reuse the normalization (null/blank -> treat as absent) but NOT the empty-string-passthrough trick: owner search passes "" to a prefix query where empty-prefix matches all; here the match is whole-name equality, so passing "" would match no specialty. Blank must route to findAll, not to the filter query with an empty argument.

Derived-query precedent: findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) returning Page. The new VetRepository method is the same shape with IgnoreCase equality instead of StartingWith, and an association traversal in the property path.

risks.risk: Filter semantic (the match) leaking into the controller would breach the Web controller row (no business rule in controllers; the existing deviation does not extend to new rules).
risks.mitigation: Keep the match in the repository derived query (IgnoreCase whole-name equality). The controller does only request adaptation - strip whitespace, treat blank as absent, branch to the right repository call, select the view - which is within the Web controller row and matches the owner-search precedent.

risks.risk: Cache inflation: both findAll overloads carry @Cacheable("vets"); a filtered method annotated the same way adds one cache entry per (specialty[, page]) argument tuple with no eviction (Open Question 5). Keys are argument-derived so filtered and unfiltered results do not collide.
risks.mitigation: For a demonstration this is acceptable and consistent with the existing pattern - annotate the new methods @Cacheable("vets") to match. If the implementer prefers not to cache the filtered path, leaving the new methods uncached is also correct and lower-risk; either is in-bounds. Do not introduce eviction here - that is the standing open question, out of this slice's scope.

risks.risk: No-match must be HTTP 200 with an empty list, not an error.
risks.mitigation: A derived findBy returns an empty Page/Collection for no match; the HTML handler renders the ordinary vetList view with an empty listVets and the JSON handler returns an empty Vets wrapper. No rejection path is added, so both surfaces answer 200 naturally. Input reaches the DB only through the parameterized derived query, so the query-param trust boundary carries no injection exposure and Thymeleaf escapes any echoed value.

notes: Verdict minor. Doc-sync follow-up (post-implementation, not done here to avoid asserting links for unwritten code): wire Implements REQ-VET-003 onto the VetController, Vets, and VetRepository rows in system-design.md § Contracts, and note the specialty filter in the VetController/VetRepository purpose text. Test guidance: the existing VetControllerTests use @MockitoBean VetRepository with MockMvc (the sanctioned controller-test mock); the new tests stub findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase for the held-specialty and no-match cases and assert the unfiltered path still calls findAll when the param is blank/absent - covering the six prd-entry test_names across both surfaces. No design-doc-autofix records present since prior dispatch; audit skipped.

author: feature-implementer
summary: Vet directory specialty filter delivered on both surfaces. VetRepository gains findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String,Pageable) and findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) (whole-name, case-insensitive equality; a prefix matches nothing by construction). VetController threads a normalized specialty param through both handlers, routing blank/whitespace/absent to findAll and non-blank to the filter query. vetList.html pagination links carry the filter forward past page 1. 8 controller tests cover both surfaces and PRD edge cases 3-5; 80 tests pass.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Untrusted specialty parameter reaches the repository only through Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase), which bind the value as a JPQL parameter — no SQL/JPQL injection

Specialty value is rendered only inside Thymeleaf link expressions (@{/vets.html(...,specialty=${specialty})}), which URL-encode parameters and HTML-attribute-escape th:href output; the value is never emitted as unescaped element text — no reflected XSS. The change also replaced the prior string-concatenated URL form with the safe parameterized link expression

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Both new `findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase` methods are missing `@Cacheable("vets")`. The existing `findAll()` and `findAll(Pageable)` are both annotated, and `system-design.md` line 103 documents VetRepository as having 'results are cached'; line 218 states 'the vet repository's read methods are cached with no eviction configured'. The new filter methods are read methods under that definition. A future maintainer will have no basis to determine whether the omission is intentional or accidental, and filtered requests will bypass the cache on every call.
findings.fix: Add `@Cacheable("vets")` above each `findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase` declaration, matching the placement on the existing `findAll` methods.

findings.description: Both new `findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase` methods omit `throws DataAccessException`. The two existing `findAll` methods both declare it, and the class-level Javadoc links to the Spring Data naming-conventions reference that governs this interface. Omitting the checked exception on only the new methods makes the interface's error contract look intentionally different for filtered queries when it is not.
findings.fix: Add `throws DataAccessException` to both `findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase` method signatures.

findings.description: `aSpecialtyPrefixShouldMatchNoVet` names an outcome ('matches no vet') but the test body asserts routing behavior: it captures the argument forwarded to the repository and checks `specialty.getValue().isEqualTo("rad")`. The empty-list result is a mock stub, not a verified assertion. A future reader will expect a list-emptiness check and find none, then wonder whether the test is incomplete.
findings.fix: Rename the method to describe what it actually asserts, e.g. `aSpecialtyPrefixIsForwardedVerbatimToTheWholeNameQuery`.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Edge case 4 (no-match returns empty + 200) is covered on the HTML surface by aSpecialtyMatchingNoVetShouldReturnAnEmptyDirectory but has no companion test on the JSON surface. The PRD mandates 'on both surfaces' for this edge case. A test stubbing findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase("dentistry") to return an empty collection on the JSON route and asserting status 200 and $.vetList.length() == 0 is missing. Without it, a regression where the JSON handler errors or returns 404 on no-match goes undetected.

Edge case 3 (case-insensitive and prefix-no-match semantics) is pinned with ArgumentCaptor on the HTML surface only (theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchTheWholeNameCaseInsensitively and aSpecialtyPrefixShouldMatchNoVet both capture against the paged overload). The PRD mandates 'either surface is filtered to it' for case-insensitive matching. Two corresponding captor tests are missing for the JSON surface: one capturing the mixed-case value forwarded to findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) and one capturing the prefix value, each verifying the controller forwards the raw stripped value verbatim to the non-paged overload.

The PRD's edge case 3 guarantee — a value matching only the start of a specialty name matches no veterinarian — is never verified at the persistence layer. Controller-level tests confirm the correct derived query method is invoked with the correct argument, but no @DataJpaTest seeds a vet with specialty 'radiology' and asserts that findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase("rad", pageable) returns an empty page and findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase("radiology", pageable) returns that vet against real H2. The implementer explicitly flagged this gap; a @DataJpaTest on VetRepository is the prescribed follow-up to make the IgnoreCase-equality derived query semantics executable as part of the suite.

recommendations: The @DataJpaTest gap (finding 3) is the highest-value follow-up: it is the only executable proof that the Spring Data derived query name encodes equality (not StartingWith) and that H2 applies case-insensitive matching — both central to REQ-VET-003's semantic contract.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Both new query methods carry @Cacheable("vets"), so the cache key now derives from the user-supplied `specialty` request parameter reaching /vets.html and /vets. The `vets` cache is created with a bare MutableConfiguration and no size or eviction bound (CacheConfiguration.cacheConfiguration(); its own comment notes the size limit must be set via the JCache implementation and it is not). Before this change the `vets` keyspace was bounded: findAll() is one key and findAll(Pageable) is keyed by page count. This PR is the first to key that unbounded cache on arbitrary attacker-controlled free text, so an attacker can enumerate distinct specialty values (?specialty=aaa1, aaa2, ...) to grow the cache without limit — a newly-introduced memory-exhaustion / availability weakness, not a pre-existing documented condition. Impact is availability only (no injection, XSS, data exposure, or auth impact); the specialty binds as a JPQL parameter and renders only inside URL-encoded Thymeleaf link expressions. Needs a human decision on caching policy: bound the vets cache (JCache-impl size limit / TTL), drop @Cacheable on the two filtered queries, or validate the specialty against the known Specialty set before querying and accept the residual risk as documented.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Both match-verifying assertions use AssertJ `contains("Leary")` (open-membership: passes when Leary appears anywhere in the result set, even among additional unexpected vets) rather than `containsExactly` or `containsExactlyInAnyOrder`. The testing-principles.md checklist prescribes `containsExactly`, `containsExactlyInAnyOrder`, and `hasSize` for collection assertions. The weaker form would not catch a regression where `findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase` returns additional vets beyond the one holding the specialty — a silent widening. The seed data happens to produce only one result, masking the gap at runtime.
findings.fix: Replace both occurrences: `assertThat(matches).extracting(Vet::getLastName).containsExactly("Leary")` on line 51 (paged overload) and line 65 (collection overload). `containsExactlyInAnyOrder` is equally correct if query-result ordering is not guaranteed by the seed data, but with a single-element result either form works.
